record.title: Neural Clustering Processes
Neural Clustering Processes
record.reason: Include: primary scientific application is neural spike sorting in Section 8, Figures 6–7, using real, synthetic and hybrid multielectrode recordings and comparison with Kilosort and variational mixtures. The method addresses low-SNR neural waveforms and posterior uncertainty in neuronal assignments. Section 5 Gaussian and MNIST mixture examples illustrate generic posterior behavior, whereas the dedicated scientific validation is neuroscience. Training on synthetic spikes and lack of ground truth for unlabeled real spikes limit claims; this is basic neuroscience methodology, not clinical validation. Supplement D–E validates on a 49-channel, 20-minute retinal recording with white-noise stimulus: receptive-field plausibility yielded 103 clear-RF templates for NCP versus 72 for Kilosort; hybrid injected templates were recovered 13/20 versus 8/20 and 6/20. Unlabeled real data use physiological plausibility rather than known neuronal identities; the implemented pipeline does not address electrode drift.
